\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{દાવો} (dāvo)}{દાવો (dāvo)}]{\gu{દાવો} (dāvo) — a claim}

\label{lesson:GU-C344-davo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for in agreement, then the Gujarati for to lean towards.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{દાવો}}
\textbf{\gu{દાવો}} — \emph{dāvo} — \textquotedblleft{}a claim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{દુકાનદારનો} \gu{દાવો} \gu{છે} \gu{કે} \gu{માલ} \gu{અસલી} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndārno dāvo che ke māl aslī che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper claims the goods are genuine.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{દાવો}} (\emph{dāvo}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{daʿwā}, \textquotedblleft{}a claim, a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāvo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāvo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndārno dāvo che ke māl aslī che.} — The shopkeeper claims the goods are genuine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for in agreement, then the Gujarati for to lean towards, then say \emph{dāvo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{દાવો} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A claim\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સાબિતી} (sābitī)}{સાબિતી (sābitī)}]{\gu{સાબિતી} (sābitī) — proof}

\label{lesson:GU-C344-sabiti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to lean towards, then the Gujarati for a claim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સાબિતી}}
\textbf{\gu{સાબિતી}} — \emph{sābitī} — \textquotedblleft{}proof\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તમારા} \gu{દાવાની} \gu{સાબિતી} \gu{ક્યાં} \gu{છે}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tamārā dāvānī sābitī kyā̃ che?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Where is the proof of your claim?
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સાબિતી}} (\emph{sābitī}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{thābit}, \textquotedblleft{}firm, proven\textquotedblright{}, which came through Persian; Gujarati adds the ending \emph{-ī} to make the noun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sābitī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sābitī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamārā dāvānī sābitī kyā̃ che?} — Where is the proof of your claim?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to lean towards, then the Gujarati for a claim, then say \emph{sābitī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ખાતરી} (khātrī)}{ખાતરી (khātrī)}]{\gu{ખાતરી} (khātrī) — an assurance; being sure}

\label{lesson:GU-C344-khatri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a claim, then the Gujarati for proof.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ખાતરી}}
\textbf{\gu{ખાતરી}} — \emph{khātrī} — \textquotedblleft{}an assurance; being sure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મને} \gu{ખાતરી} \gu{છે} \gu{કે} \gu{તે} \gu{સમયસર} \gu{આવશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mane khātrī che ke te samaysar āvśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I am sure he will come on time.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ખાતરી}} (\emph{khātrī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khātir}, \textquotedblleft{}the mind, regard\textquotedblright{}, a word of Arabic origin, with the Gujarati ending \emph{-ī}; \textquotedblleft{}being sure\textquotedblright{} is the Gujarati sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khātrī}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a claim, then the Gujarati for proof, then say \emph{khātrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સંદેહ} (sandeh)}{સંદેહ (sandeh)}]{\gu{સંદેહ} (sandeh) — uncertainty; a lingering doubt}

\label{lesson:GU-C344-sandeh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for proof, then the Gujarati for an assurance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સંદેહ}}
\textbf{\gu{સંદેહ}} — \emph{sandeh} — \textquotedblleft{}uncertainty; a lingering doubt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{આ} \gu{પરિણામ} \gu{સાચું} \gu{છે} \gu{તેમાં} \gu{કોઈ} \gu{સંદેહ} \gu{નથી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā pariṇām sācũ che temā̃ koī sandeh nathī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is no doubt that this result is right.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સંદેહ}} (\emph{sandeh}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{saṃdeha}, \textquotedblleft{}a doubt, uncertainty\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sandeh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sandeh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā pariṇām sācũ che temā̃ koī sandeh nathī.} — There is no doubt that this result is right.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for proof, then the Gujarati for an assurance, then say \emph{sandeh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{સંદેહ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Uncertainty; a lingering doubt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{દર્શાવવું} (darśāvvũ)}{દર્શાવવું (darśāvvũ)}]{\gu{દર્શાવવું} (darśāvvũ) — to indicate}

\label{lesson:GU-C344-darsavvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for an assurance, then the Gujarati for uncertainty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{દર્શાવવું}}
\textbf{\gu{દર્શાવવું}} — \emph{darśāvvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to indicate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{આ} \gu{ફોટો} \gu{દર્શાવે} \gu{છે} \gu{કે} \gu{દુકાન} \gu{રાત્રે} \gu{ખુલ્લી} \gu{હતી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā phoṭo darśāve che ke dukān rātre khullī hatī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This photo shows that the shop was open at night.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{સાબિતી} \gu{દર્શાવી}, \emph{teṇe sābitī darśāvī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{દર્શાવવું}} (\emph{darśāvvũ}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{darśana}, \textquotedblleft{}seeing, showing\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Gujarati causative ending \emph{-āvvũ}: to make something seen.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darśāvvũ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for an assurance, then the Gujarati for uncertainty, then say \emph{darśāvvũ} again
\end{itemize}
